note: Every cheap question that must be answered YES before a push runs. Add a gate here instead of editing a script: code/gates.py runs this list and code/check_all.sh calls it after its own built-in invariant checks (ASCII .ps1, branch guard, script copies, loop summaries). severity=block stops the push, warn only prints. plane=local marks a gate only the user's machine can answer - listed so the plan stays complete, skipped by the sandbox runner. Gate list is data: add one entry to extend it. The task-agnostic runner (code/local_loop.py) reads code/recipes/<id>.json; this list is what it runs as the 'gates' step, so a repo's own checks live here too.

gates.why: the deck pages read their numbers out of the repo, so one input can build a page whose module boxes overlap - the machine's checker rejects that page and the whole round fails (round 28)
an acceptance needle that no file in the worktree contains fails the round on the machine even when every local check passed (round 33)
the installable skill carries the loop's code inside itself; if that copy drifts, another session installs an old loop
the task recipe is what tells the machine what to build and verify - a malformed recipe must fail here, not mid-round
the local plane itself: the real install / real Office / real GUI check, run by the watcher on the user's machine as sections 3 and 4 of code/local_check.ps1 (or local_check.sh on Linux)
